about: The MCP clients whose client ID metadata documents (CIMD, the MCP spec's Client ID Metadata Documents; 6E3c, AG5) the API fetches, in one place. Where Agent X's OAuth server is on (staging), the foundation opens the apps subnet's way out to each one's addresses on 443 (network.bicep) and lets the network look up its host (dns-policy.bicep), and the apps deployment puts its origin on the API's outbound allowlist and its entry on AGENTX_OAUTH_CLIENT_METADATA_ORIGINS (apps.bicep); elsewhere, none of it. Adding a client is one entry here: `metadata` is what the API trusts, its document's exact address or the tightest path prefix its documents sit under (never a whole origin where the host serves anyone else's content: claude.ai serves people's own), written as the setting takes it (https, lowercase, as the URL parser prints it); `prefixes` are the IPv4 ranges its host answers from, as its owner publishes them, with `source` saying where; the host's name is read from `metadata`. A daily check (mcp-watch.yml, `node deploy/azure/mcp-clients.ts`) warns when a host answers outside its ranges. Any client not listed registers itself (RFC 7591, DCR), as every client could before. Not listed on purpose: clients behind a shared front such as Cloudflare (ChatGPT, chatgpt.com): its ranges carry a large share of the web, so opening them would let the subnet reach every site there by address. Those keep registering until the way out can name hosts (an egress proxy, or a firewall's FQDN rule: AZ22). The API's own guards stay as they are (oauth-client-metadata.ts): only listed addresses fetched, only origins on its allowlist, no redirect followed, 3 seconds and 16 KB at most. Checked by mcp-clients.test.ts and the policy's apps-egress and dns-allow rules.

clients.source: Anthropic's published inbound addresses, which claude.ai answers from: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/ip-addresses (checked 19 Nov 2026); the document's address as Claude names itself in it (client_id, read 19 Nov 2026)
